subject: Missing soma type in read/written neurons from CATMAID

messages.author: e5958e7785943528
messages.subject: Missing soma type in read/written neurons from CATMAID
parts:
Hi,

This one is hard to pin down where the change has occurred but previously when loading neurons from catmaid, aligning and saving to SWC the soma point was labelled with the appropriate SWC type. 

It's worth noting previously we had to also scale the radius from nm->um manually this seems to now be handled automatically - so thanks to whoever fixed that.

However now the soma point is marked with a 0 type (undefined) as most of all the other nodes instead of 1 (soma) as had previously been the case.

Has something changed in how soma points are interpreted or should I be looking for changes in the catmaid API?

Any help you can give would be appreciated, Thanks,

Rob Court

messages.author: e5958e7785943528
messages.subject: Re: Missing soma type in read/written neurons from CATMAID
parts:
and the moment I submit this I have found my answer; the soma point in the compact-skeleton export is wrong so I will pursue this with catmaid.

FYI we are using the current dev version as we needed new features so should hopefully be fixed before it hits the main release.

parts:
And I'm back again. Was mistaken the id is correct but doesn't seem to be allocated correctly in nat?

in https://fafb.catmaid.virtualflybrain.org//1/16/1/1/compact-skeleton%3Chttps://fafb.catmaid.virtualflybrain.org/1/16/1/1/compact-skeleton the soma is given as:
Soma: [
2941309
],

With that point being (correctly):
[
2941309,
null,
4,
451291.66,
205574.2,
23800,
4039,
5
]

But in the SWC the soma point is applied to:
[
         72,
         71,
         4,
         476775.72,
         146627.03,
         170320,
         -1,
         5
]
in swc:
head 16.swc
# SWC format file
# based on specifications at http://www.neuronland.org/NLMorphologyConverter/MorphologyFormats/SWC/Spec.html
# Created by nat::write.neuron.swc
# PointNo Label X Y Z Radius Parent
1 0 451291.66 205574.2 23800 4039 -1
2 0 450696.5 209644.72 23400 -1 1
3 0 450653.78 210062.67 23080 -1 2
4 0 451839.1 210611.47 22800 -1 3

With the only line with a soma type being:
cat 16.swc | grep " 1 "
1566 1 476775.72 146627.03 170320 -1 1565

The load and save was done using:
remotes::install_github("natverse/rcatmaid")
remotes::install_github("natverse/natverse")
library(catmaid)
conn=catmaid_login(server="https://fafb.catmaid.virtualflybrain.org")
library(natverse)
swc=read.neurons.catmaid("16")
write.neurons(swc, dir="~/FAFB", format='swc', normalise.ids=TRUE, Force=TRUE)
